clue.text: Thinking it may be dead

definitions.meaning: dead ... is navigation by speed, time and heading alone

explanation.definitionFit: Calculation is a kind of thinking, and navigators' dead reckoning fixes position without landmarks.

clue.text: In the red having lost one's : skill

explanation.definitionFit: Reddish brown like corroded iron, and out of practice.

clue.text: Kind of Saint

explanation.definitionFit: A merciful person is lenient, and several saints and popes bore the name.

clue.text: His recognized merit makes man burgeon. Official

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
to bud is to burgeon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man honoured for merit flourishes and becomes a public figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to investigate public complaints.

clue.text: A combine in sheep feed

parts.note: taken as written
a teg is a sheep in its second year
a ration is an allowance of feed

explanation.surface: A combine harvester used to feed sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining parts into a whole is integration.

clue.text: What's in it can chew it

definitions.text: What's in it can chew it

parts.words: What's in it can chew it
parts.note: the teeth set in this mouth tissue can chew the sticky sweet of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both the flesh round the teeth and the stuff chewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouth tissue holding the teeth, and chewing confection.

clue.text: Last yell 'of man-eaten ?

parts.note: the final cry of someone being devoured would name the big cat doing it; also, an extra shout tacked on after three cheers bears the same name

explanation.walkthrough: In old American cheering, the 'tiger' was a final yell after the cheers, so the clue's two senses meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating big cat of India, and the final howl added to a round of cheers.

clue.text: Make a fool into a poet

annotationWithheld.why: 'Make a fool into a poet (5)': ASS inside TO gives TASSO, but TO only comes from 'into', which is also the container signal: one word doing two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Make a fool into a poet

clue.text: If I'm in a blessed state why the wry look?

indicators.note: 'in' puts the letters of I'm inside the holy state

parts.note: a state of grace is blessed
I'm without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they pull a face when supposedly blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted facial expression of distaste.

clue.text: The Mirror for the thinking man

definitions.meaning: a looking glass, or the newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A mirror throws light back, and a pondering person reflects.

clue.text: Refreshing's her flutter

definitions.note: used as a noun, a refreshing drink or sweet

parts.note: the 's gives S
taken as written
a flutter is a small bet

explanation.surface: Someone finds a little gamble on the horses refreshing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy powder or iced drink taken as a refreshment.

clue.text: Not cross, Noel, yet has a quarrel with Barker

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave the cross out of the festive word

parts.note: Noel is Christmas, written XMAS
X is a cross shape
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone called Noel is not angry, yet argues with a man named Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like a surname but is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A large guard dog breed, and dogs are barkers.

clue.text: Give in return

definitions.meaning: a return on an investment, the profit made

explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give in, and a crop or dividend is the return produced.

clue.text: Boast of heat and light company to refit a den

parts.note: gas supplies heat and, in old homes, light

indicators.note: refitting rebuilds the letters of 'a den' in a new order

explanation.surface: A gas utility boasts about renovating a den.
explanation.definitionFit: Boastful bragging, named after the Gascons, famed as braggarts.

clue.text: Cold cat of Oz

definitions.meaning: a big cat of the cold high mountains
oz is ounce, another name for this cat

explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan big cat also called the ounce, abbreviated oz.

clue.text: Nonsense! It's dry in a house

definitions.meaning: a fungal decay of timber in buildings

explanation.definitionFit: Talking rubbish is talking nonsense, and dry rot is the timber decay found in houses.

clue.text: Getting one's hooks on a USA crop one organized

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for greed, matching an adjective

indicators.note: organized means the letters are set into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a share of an American harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy, grasping, like a bird of prey with hooked claws.

clue.text: Nature's cure for acid pastures?

parts.note: seems to be about liming sour fields, but the 'sweet' of fields is a wild herb used against stomach acid

explanation.walkthrough: Fields are MEADOWS and the opposite of acid is SWEET, so the herb's name itself sounds like a cure for sour pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild plant of damp meadows, a folk remedy for indigestion and source of salicylic compounds.

clue.text: So to retired bay-Ena's changed and gets a crop

indicators.note: retired means going backwards, so bay runs right to left
changed means the letters of Ena's are rearranged

parts.note: Ena's with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Ena retires to the bay and grows a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes grown in fields as a major food and oil crop.

clue.text: Goriot comes to retired pub with pal as a regular

parts.note: Pere Goriot is Balzac's novel, so Goriot is Pere

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the pub's letters run backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an ally is a pal

explanation.surface: Balzac's old father goes to his local with a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Year after year, always, which is doing something as a regular thing.

clue.text: As this hind said to loving mate in boat?

indicators.note: said means it is the spoken form that counts

parts.note: an oarsman's request 'row, dear'

explanation.surface: A deer speaks lovingly to its partner in a rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European deer, whose female is a doe or hind.

clue.text: Mark loan unit

parts.note: the organ that comes before 'mark' to make a word for a reserved sign, and the one Mark Antony asks friends to lend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lend me your ears' makes the organ a unit of loan; it is also what goes before 'mark'.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing, lent in Shakespeare and prefixed to a sign of ownership.

clue.text: Mrs Adam takes up dyestuff that's novel

parts.note: Eve was Adam's wife

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word runs bottom to top

parts.note: anil is indigo dye

explanation.surface: Eve takes up dyeing, which is new.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanny Burney's 1778 novel is titled with this name.

clue.text: Player's in crease, in a word, so someone's scored

definitions.text: Player's in crease, in a word, so someone's scored

parts.words: Player's in crease, in a word, so someone's scored
parts.note: the batsman 'in crease', run together into one word, means a growth in volume, which is marked in a musical score

explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (a batsman safe in the crease, a run scored) hides 'increase', a direction in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical marking for gradually louder playing, an increase in volume.

clue.text: Good thing he's dead, said Clerihew

definitions.text: Good thing he's dead, said Clerihew

parts.words: Good thing he's dead, said Clerihew
parts.note: E C Bentley's first clerihew says what he likes about this man is that he is no longer alive

explanation.walkthrough: Clerihew was Bentley's middle name; his verse on Robert Clive of India praises him for being dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Clive, subject of the first comic four-line verse by Bentley.

clue.text: Note what's left of French naval base

parts.note: B is a musical note
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: A remark on what remains of the French navy's station.
explanation.definitionFit: A port in Brittany, a major French navy harbour.

clue.text: Jumbo projects ?

parts.note: seems to mean huge schemes but means the ivory parts projecting from an elephant

explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo is an elephant's nickname and projects are parts sticking out.
explanation.definitionFit: Long projecting ivory teeth of an elephant.

clue.text: Debouching into round enclosure in the Greek capital

parts.note: O is a round shape
a pen is an enclosure for animals
taken as written

indicators.note: a capital letter here is the initial of the next word

explanation.surface: A river empties into a circular yard in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A street debouching into a square is one opening onto it.

clue.text: A hiatus in the return of the " Clowns "

indicators.note: return means the short name runs back to front

parts.note: Pag is short for Pagliacci, the opera whose title means clowns

explanation.surface: A pause in the comeback of a famous troupe of circus clowns.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera fans pair 'Cav and Pag'; I Pagliacci means The Clowns.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an interruption or break, a hiatus.

clue.text: One lying among the pineapples

indicators.note: lying among places the single letter within the fruit word

parts.note: ananas is a word for pineapples
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stretched out in a pineapple plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Ananias was the biblical liar, so 'one lying'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical Ananias was struck dead for lying, so his name means a liar.

clue.text: Loose stones somewhat owl like in their sound

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the owl noise is kept

parts.note: the barn owl's cry is a screech

explanation.surface: Loose stones rattling down a slope make a noise like an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose rock fragments on a mountain slope.

clue.text: The standing of great men with feet of clay ?

definitions.text: The standing of great men with feet of clay ?

parts.words: The standing of great men with feet of clay ?
parts.note: statues of great men stand on bases, and a statue with feet of clay is the biblical idol of flawed greatness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' seems to mean reputation but means what statues literally stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: Bases on which statues of the great stand.
